BadRequest.description: The request body or parameters are malformed or fail validation.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the resource's current state.

Forbidden.description: The caller is authenticated but lacks the capability or access this needs.

IdempotencyKeyReused.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different request (type `problems/idempotency-key-reused`).

InternalServerError.description: The server failed while handling the request; the `X-Request-Id` response header names it in the server log.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or the caller cannot see it.

Overloaded.description: The server is at its in-flight request ceiling (`MAIDAN_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`) and refused the request without running it; retry after `Retry-After`.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body exceeds the server's body-size limit (`MAIDAN_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, or `MAIDAN_ARTIFACT_MAX_BODY_BYTES` for an artifact upload).

TooManyRequests.description: A rate limit or a per-token capability quota is exhausted.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate-limit window resets. Sent by the per-client and per-workspace rate limits, not by a per-token capability quota.

Unauthorized.description: The credential is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body is not declared as JSON; send `Content-Type: application/json`.

AcceptedDecision.description:
A token-lean view of a closed/archived in-channel decision, for the next
`claim_next` claimer's context pack. Deliberately **not** the full
`ThreadResult` JSON — `rendered` / findings stay on `GET
/threads/:id/result`. `result_kind` is a **namespaced schema string** (e.g.
`example.review.result/1`), never a closed enum.

result_kind.description:
Namespaced producer schema (e.g. `example.review.result/1`). Absent on opaque
JSON that does not carry a string `result_kind`.

AccountedUsageRequest.description:
Caller-supplied economic evidence for one retry-safe usage heartbeat.

The thread comes from the REST path or MCP tool envelope. The reporter and
payer are deliberately absent: Maidan derives them from authentication and
the resolved thread. `model` is the model id the response named.

AcknowledgeClaim.description:
Acknowledge a claim and start the working clock. The current holder presents
its fencing token; the working clock (`work_started_at`) is stamped once and
preserved on re-acknowledge.

ActiveClaim.description: A live claim and the footprint it holds.

attributes.description:
The claimed thread's task attributes; the defaults when the thread
was never described.

lease_expires_at.description: `None` for a claim taken without a lease, which holds until released.

oneOf.description: `member` (default) or `admin`.

AddReviewer.description: Name a reviewer for a thread — the eligible set (empty = open review).

AddSkill.description: Add a skill — to a member (`declares`) or a thread (`requires`).

AddThreadDependency.description:
Add a task-dependency edge — the thread in the path depends on
`depends_on_thread_id`.

AllowEgressTarget.description:
Bless an external destination for egress. `selector` must be an **id**: a
Slack channel id (`C…`/`G…`), or a GitHub repository `owner/name` — not a
`#channel-name`, and not `owner/name#123`. A name is mutable, so an
allowlist keyed on one is not an allowlist; and on GitHub the operator
blesses the repository, since per-issue blessing would mean a ticket per PR.

AllowSecretEgressHost.description:
Trust a host with the workspace's secret values: a lowercase hostname or
IPv4 address, with no scheme, port or path.

AllowedEgressTarget.description:
A destination a workspace's operator has blessed for egress.

`surface` is stored as text rather than an [`EgressSurface`], for the same
reason [`EgressOutbox`] does: a row written by a newer build and read after
a downgrade must still be *listable*, or the operator cannot see the entry
they need to revoke. The write side is typed ([`NewEgressTarget`]), so a
surface this build cannot deliver to can never be blessed in the first
place.

dead.description:
Why this entry can no longer authorize anything, when it can't: a row
written before a rule tightened (a non-ASCII branch, a ref spelling) or
by a newer build stays listable so the operator can revoke it, and this
says it is dead. Absent on a live entry.

AmendPlan.description:
A change to a submitted plan, made in one transaction by the planner
holding the parent's claim: cancel unclaimed children, add children, and
rewire the dependencies of unclaimed ones. A key that is cancelled and
added in the same amendment is replaced: its dependents wait for the new
child instead.

add.description:
Children to add; their `depends_on` may name any key the amended
plan keeps. Linted as `submit_plan`'s children are.

cancel.description: Keys of unclaimed children to cancel.

reason.description: Why, on each cancelled child's notice.

AnswerApprovalGate.description:
Answer a human-approval gate: accept / decline / cancel, with the HMAC
`request_state` the server issued alongside the pending gate.

action.description:
`accept`, `decline`, or `cancel`. Any other value is a bad request — an
empty or unknown action is never a silent accept.

content.description: Optional structured detail the human supplies with their decision.

request_state.description: The opaque integrity token from the pending-gate list — must verify.

ApprovalGate.description:
A durable, queryable human-approval gate. An agent's `request_approval`
opens one `Pending` gate and returns an `input-required` result instead of
blocking; a human later resolves it via the `/ui`. Persisted so the gate
survives a dropped connection and can be listed while outstanding
(queryable). An optional `thread_id` attaches the gate to a thread for the
N6 required-human claim gate.

oneOf.description:
Set when a model decided the gate through `approval_decide`, directly
or by a person confirming its request in the console. `None` for an
answer given over REST or on the console's own buttons.

The delegate that actually opened the gate for `requested_by`, when one
did. `None`: `requested_by` opened it itself.
The delegate that actually answered it for `resolved_by`, when one did.

risk.description:
How much a wrong accept would cost, as whoever opened the gate said.
`high` when it said nothing.

ApprovalGateState.description:
The state of an approval gate. A gate opens `Pending`; a human resolves it
to exactly one of accept/decline/cancel. Silence never resolves a gate
(there is no timeout auto-approve), and a resolve is a compare-and-set on
`Pending` so a double-answer can't flip it.

ApprovalGateView.description:
A pending approval gate plus the `request_state` a human echoes back to
answer it.

oneOf.description:
A model's live request, through `approval_decide`, for a person to
confirm accepting this gate. Absent when no model is waiting on one.

ApprovalPolicy.description: The confirmation threshold a workspace sets for `approval_decide`.

confirm_at.description:
The lowest gate risk at which a model's accept needs a person to
confirm it in the console. `low` (the default) means every one does.

confirm_link_ttl_seconds.description:
How long a confirmation link `approval_decide` sends lives, in
seconds: from 60 to 3600, 600 (ten minutes) by default. A link keeps
the lifetime it was sent with.

is_default.description: `true` when the workspace has set nothing and the defaults apply.

ApprovalRisk.description:
How much a wrong accept of a gate would cost. Ordered: `Low < Medium <
High`. A workspace's [`ApprovalPolicy`] names the lowest risk at which a
model's accept needs a person to confirm it.

filename.description:
The name the caller's workspace uploaded the bytes under, for display
only: it never locates anything. Another workspace holding the same
bytes sees its own name, or none. Omitted when absent, so an event
written before the field existed serializes as it was written.

ArtifactErasure.description:
One workspace's reference to a shared artifact, erased. Artifacts are
content-addressed and deduplicated across workspaces, so the bytes go only
with the last reference.

last_reference.description:
No workspace references the artifact any more: its row is gone and its
bytes are deleted from blob storage.

note.description: Optional handoff note for the assignee.

AttenuateToken.description:
Holder-side attenuation body. No `token:admin` — the caller can only drop
rights they already hold.

AttestationTier.description: How far a piece of evidence can be trusted, from strongest to weakest.

oneOf.description: Who performed the action. For a delegated action, the delegate.
The delegation grant the action was taken under, if any.
Who the action was performed for — the actor itself unless delegated.

The workspace the row belongs to: the one whose audit view shows it and
whose legal hold keeps it. `None` is an instance-level row, shown only in
the operator audit and pruned under instance policy.

AuthorizationServerMetadata.description:
RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata.

Only the grants, response type and challenge method the server implements
are listed. There is no `registration_endpoint` because clients are
pre-registered or carry a client metadata document, never registered
dynamically.

response_modes_supported.description:
Named because an omitted list means `query` and `fragment`, and the
authorization response is only ever a query string.

revocation_endpoint_auth_methods_support.description:
RFC 8414 gives no default for the revocation endpoint, so a client
learns only from this list that it authenticates there as at the
token endpoint.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description:
Named although the RFC 8414 default, `client_secret_basic`, is among
them: the list also says a public client may send no secret at all.

BlockedReason.description:
Why a thread is explicitly blocked from dispatch. A **closed** enum — unlike
`result_kind`, which is a namespaced string a producer publishes. Presence
of a [`ThreadBlock`] row is the block; absence is unblocked. Distinct/218
DAG readiness (children / deps must be terminal before `claim_next` will
pick a thread): that skip is derived from the dependency graph. This reason
is an orchestrator- set taxonomy of *why* a thread is parked from the queue.

`child` is "waiting on a child the orchestrator named", not "every DAG child
must be terminal". `unclaimable` here is the same vocabulary as the park, as
one of six reasons — the 363 side table is unchanged.

BootPack.description:
The workspace and channel layers every agent of that channel shares.
A thread pack's prefix starts with these bytes. Glossary and accepted
decisions are omitted when empty, on both this object and the thread
prefix, so the byte prefix still holds.

accepted_decisions.description:
The channel's accepted decisions, oldest first. The same list for
every thread in the channel.

BudgetPatch.description:
A partial change to a thread's budget.

[`BudgetLimits`] is a **total replace**: every dimension it does not name
becomes "no cap", and a dimension with no cap never binds. So sending
`{max_tokens}` to raise one limit silently removed the usd, turns and wall
limits — and a removed limit is a run that should have been stopped and was
not. the `deny_unknown_fields` catches a *typo*; it cannot catch a
well-formed body that simply omits a field.

Each field here distinguishes three states:

* **absent** — leave this dimension exactly as it is
* **`null`** — clear the cap on this dimension (explicitly unbounded)
* **a value** — set it

So widening always requires *saying so*: there is no spelling of a budget
change that removes a cap by omission.

BuriedDecision.description:
A decision the member may have missed — a task result produced by someone
else in a channel or thread the member follows, since their last digest. The
buried-decisions digest lists these instead of a bare unread count; it's
also queryable directly.

CancelThread.description:
Body for `POST /threads/:id/cancel`: why the task is being cancelled, 1 to
500 characters after trimming. It is posted on the thread and kept as the
dispatch park's reason.

CancelledThread.description: A cancelled thread: the closed row and why it was cancelled.

CatchUpPage.description: One page of events after a snapshot (or after a prior page).

events.description:
The whole log, sealed as it is hashed, with each live event's
`content_key` ([`crate::KeyedEvent`]).

head_lsn.description:
Workspace head at page build (`0` if empty). Live waits until
`events.last.id` (or `after_lsn` when empty) >= this.

room_lsn.description: Global room head. Not a catch-up cursor — other tenants move it.

ChainVerifyReport.description: Report from walking a chain. `ok` is the fail-closed bit.

previous_head.description:
The head a squash-rebase round force-moved the branch from: with
`commit_sha`, the range a reviewer diffs to see what the rebase
changed. `None` for a normal round.

rebase.description: Whether this round rebuilt the branch on the base's head.

ChannelFollow.description:
A member following a channel — presence = following. The notification router
notifies followers of activity in the channel, honoring mutes.

ChannelMember.description:
Membership row for a channel. Rows exist for private channels; public
channels are open to the whole workspace without rows.

ChannelMemberRole.description:
A member's role within a channel. `Admin` may manage membership; both roles
grant access to a private channel.

ChannelOccupancy.description:
The occupancy of a channel's **open** task threads — the two-clocks
refinement of [`QueueDepth`]. It splits `assigned` by the *working* clock,
so an orchestrator sees not just how much work is held but how much is
actually underway. The four sub-counts partition `open`:
- `queued`: claimable now, the [`QueueDepth::ready`] count.
- `claimed`: held on a live lease, but the holder has not yet acknowledged —
  `work_started_at` is unset (grabbed the work, hasn't started).
- `working`: held and the holder has acknowledged and begun work
  (`work_started_at` is set).
- `blocked`: not held and not claimable, [`QueueDepth::blocked`] plus
  [`QueueDepth::unclaimable`].

Splitting `claimed` from `working` is the payoff of the two clocks: it
surfaces a claimed-but-idle agent — one that took work but never started it.

ChildThreadSummary.description:
A child thread collapsed under its parent: the child thread plus a live
count of its (non-tombstoned) messages, so a threaded view can show "N
replies" without loading each child's messages.

CiStatus.description: How the checks on a pull request's head stand.

ClaimNextThread.description: Claim the next unassigned/expired thread in a channel.

oneOf.description:
Only claim a thread routed to this engine (`pi`, `session` or
`human`), for a worker that serves one kind of work. A thread routed
to another engine, or not routed at all, is then never claimed.

The service lane this worker runs in (`batch` or `flex`). Lane breaks
ties, never filters: among threads of equal priority and wait, threads
in this lane come first, then unlaned ones, then other lanes. Omitted,
unlaned threads win the tie.

lease_secs.description:
Lease in seconds (1 s to 7 days). The holder renews before it lapses;
a lapsed claim is reaped and the thread returns to the queue with a
`ClaimExpired`. Omitted, the server's default lease applies
(`MAIDAN_CLAIM_DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS`, 600 s).

repo.description:
Only claim a thread whose footprint names this repository
(`owner/name` or a GitHub clone URL), for a worker whose checkout is
that repository. A thread without a footprint is then never claimed.

ClaimThread.description:
Atomically claim an unassigned thread for a member. The claimer is both the
actor and the assignee.

ClaimedThread.description:
`claim_next` body: the claimed thread plus a content-addressed pin.
`pin` is additive; thread fields stay at the top level (`flatten`).

ClientIdentitySource.description: Where a decided-via client's name came from, strongest first.

ConfirmApprovalGate.description:
Body for `POST /auth/approval-confirmations/confirm`: the gate and the
token from a confirmation link's fragment.

ContentBlock.description:
A typed part of a message's structured content. The wire form is internally
tagged (`{"type":"text","text":"…"}`), matching the MCP / Anthropic
content-block dialect and the existing A2A `TextPart`. `body` remains the
canonical searchable plain-text projection derived from these.

oneOf.description: A tool/function invocation (agent → tool).
The result of a prior [`ContentBlock::ToolUse`], correlated by id.
A pointer to a resource/artifact (URI form).

ContextPrefix.description:
The stable part of a thread context pack, in serialization order. The
leading fields are the [`BootPack`]. A post appends to `messages` and
changes nothing before that key.

ContextTail.description: The volatile tail, serialized after the prefix.

as_of.description: The event-log id an as-of pack was rebuilt at.

ci.description:
Where the checks stand on the thread's tracked pull requests. In the
tail for the same reason as the notices: each sweep tick may rewrite
it.

notices.description:
The thread's change notices, newest first, at most 10. In the tail
because a merge elsewhere adds one without touching the thread's own
history, and the prefix must stay cache-stable.

prefix_bytes.description: Length of that prefix JSON, in bytes.

prefix_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the prefix's compact JSON, hex.

CreateAgent.description:
Body for `POST /workspaces/{wid}/agents`. There is no `kind` and no
capability list: the member is always an agent, and its token always holds
the `maidan.agent.worker` set.

handle.description: 1 to 64 characters, no whitespace. Unique in the workspace.

label.description: The token's label. Defaults to the handle.

CreateMemoryBlock.description:
Create a memory block. `label` is the block's within-workspace key; `value`
defaults to empty, `read_only` to false. Creating an existing label returns
the existing block (concurrent-safe).

content.description:
Typed structured content. When present and `body` is empty, the server
derives `body` from these blocks for search/back-compat.

remote_workspace_id.description: Workspace on the remote peer to poll; defaults to the path workspace when omitted.

CreateRecipe.description:
Create a recipe blueprint. `spec` is the `RecipeSpec` (params, definition of
done, retry, inline DAG children).

relation.description:
Typed relation. Snake_case string; controlled set
`RelationKind::CONTROLLED`, unknown values round-trip via `Other`.

CreateSecret.description:
Create (or rotate) a named secret. The `value` is encrypted at rest and
never returned by `list` — only by `resolve`.

CreateTaskSchedule.description:
Create a task schedule. When due, the sweeper creates a thread titled
`title` in `channel_id`. `interval_secs` omitted (or null) = one-shot; a
positive value = recurring. `first_run_at` omitted = fire on the next tick
(defaults to now).

recipe_id.description:
When set, each firing instantiates this recipe (parent + DAG children)
instead of creating one bare thread.

description.description: What the task is about, in the creator's words.

oneOf.description:
The task's claim footprint, stored with the thread so the claim queue
never sees it without one: the producer declares it at intake under
the `workspace:write` that creating the thread needs. Refining it
later is `PUT /threads/{id}/footprint`.

priority.description:
The thread's dispatch priority (higher is more urgent; the default is
0), stored with the thread under the creator's `workspace:write`.
Changing it later is `PUT /threads/{id}/priority`.

confidence.description:
Optional confidence weight, by convention in `0..=1`, for weighted
consensus. Omit to state no confidence.

kind.description: `approve`, `request_changes`, or `ack`. Any other kind is a 400.

DeadEgress.description:
A dead-lettered delivery for the operator DLQ view: a message that exhausted
its retries, or whose link was disabled as misconfigured. `last_error` is
why the final attempt failed — the surface's own words.

DeclaredStatus.description:
An agent's self-reported status on a thread. Distinct from [`ThreadState`]
(the workflow FSM) — this is what the agent says it's doing. `Stalled` is
system-computed only and cannot be declared.

DeferralReason.description: Why the claim queue is holding a thread back.

DeferredThread.description: A thread the claim queue would otherwise hand out, and why it waits.

capabilities.description:
Optional further attenuation. Empty uses the intersection of the
grant and the delegate's current authority.

DelegationPolicy.description: A workspace's delegation policy: the longest a grant may live.

is_default.description: `true` when the workspace has set nothing and the default applies.

DeliveryModeView.description: A member's current email delivery mode.

DlqEntry.description:
A dead-lettered agent run. When a claimed run is stopped because it exceeded
its budget envelope, the claim fails and a DLQ entry is recorded — so the
failed work is triageable (retry, raise the budget, give up) rather than
silently lost or silently marked done. Captures the failure snapshot: which
thread, which agent, why, and usage at the moment of failure.

member_id.description: The agent whose run was stopped.

content.description: Replacement structured content. Omitted → keep existing.

EgressSurface.description:
An external surface a projector can deliver to. Lowercase identifiers, as in
the `deliver_to` grammar pinned in `docs/Result Delivery.md`.

EmailDeliveryMode.description:
How a member wants notification emails delivered. The default (an absent
preference row) is `Immediate` — the behaviour. `Digest` opts out of
per-notification emails in favour of a periodic rollup from the digest
sweeper; the two are mutually exclusive by design.

oneOf.description: The engine the tasks were routed to; `None` for tasks never routed.

EngineRollup.description: The tasks routed to one engine.

applied.description: Whether the pull request carries the label now.

EscalationPolicy.description:
What a thread wait does when its deadline lapses. **Never a decision** — the
"TimedOut ≠ Decline" rule: a timeout must not invent a human refusal (or
approval). Both variants emit a `WaitTimedOut` event (the notification
router then reaches the thread's owner); `Park` additionally marks the
thread unclaimable so `claim_next` won't dispatch a stuck thread until a
human intervenes.

EventLink.description: One log row's chain fields. `lsn` equals `id`.

EvidenceAttestation.description: One piece of evidence and the tier it was given at the hand-off.

attested_by.description:
Who put it there: the result's producer, the artifact's linker, or the
pass's recorder.

EvidenceKind.description: What kind of evidence an attestation is about.

EvidenceManifest.description:
The evidence a thread put in front of its reviewers when it went to review:
its result and its linked artifacts, each by content hash. Messages are the
conversation around the evidence, not the evidence, so a comment after an
approval does not undo it. No timestamps, so recomputing it from unchanged
evidence gives the same root on either backend.

attestations.description:
How far each piece of evidence can be trusted, judged once at the
hand-off and part of the root, so an approval names the tiers it was
shown as well as the evidence. Empty on packets recorded before tiers
existed, which serialize (and so hash) exactly as they did.

evidence_changed_since_review.description:
Whether the result or the linked artifacts differ from what the
latest review packet was handed. `None` before any hand-off.
Messages are not evidence, so a comment does not set it.

thread_version.description:
The thread's version now; each `review_requested` entry carries the
version it was handed at.

EvidenceTimelineEntry.description: One recorded piece of evidence, or one step of its review.

oneOf.description: An artifact was linked to the thread.

The thread's current result was recorded. A result is overwritten
when re-set, so only the standing one is on the timeline; a review
packet keeps the hash of the one it was handed.

sha256.description:
The hash a review packet pins the result by; `None` only if the
stored result could not be canonicalized.

oneOf.description: A land-gate verdict was recorded.
The thread was handed to review with this packet.
A reviewer gave a verdict.

ExportPublicKey.description:
`GET /operator/export-public-key` — out-of-band pin for a destination
instance's `MAIDAN_EXPORT_VERIFY_KEYS`.

FleetConformance.description: A workspace's recent completed reports against a fleet profile.

conforms.description: Whether every report read conforms. True when there are none.

FleetDivergence.description:
One divergent value and how many of the member's reports carried it.
`seen` is absent when the report sent no value (or, for the boot pack, did
not list it).

FleetField.description: The profile field a report diverged on.

FleetProfile.description:
The published build a fleet runs. Every field is optional; an unset field
is not checked.

boot_pack_sha256.description: sha256, hex, of the boot pack every call must list in `pack_sha256`.

repo.description: `owner/name`, lowercase; a GitHub clone URL is accepted and reduced to it.

FootprintConflict.description: One item of a live claim that a footprint would overlap.

FreezeMember.description: Freeze a member — the kill-switch. `reason` is an optional audit note.

FreezeResult.description:
The result of freezing a member: the freeze record + the number of active
claims released (leases dropped).

GateDecisionVia.description:
Which MCP client a model decided a gate through, and that a model asked.
`client_source` says how far the name can be trusted: `credential` names
what the token was issued to (and `client_id` is its id), `self_reported`
is what the client called itself in `clientInfo` (a label for the record,
never a credential), and `none` means the request named no client.

client_id.description:
The credential client's id. Set only when `client_source` is
`credential`.

model_asked.description:
Always `true` on a recorded decision: the tool is only ever called by
a model. Kept as a field so the record says it, not the reader.

GenAiUsageReport.description:
One OpenTelemetry-style usage report. Token counts come from the GenAI
attributes; the price snapshot is still the reporter's, because Maidan
keeps no rate card. `usd_micros` is computed, not trusted.

evidence.description: Wins over the same field inferred from `attributes`.

GithubIssueLink.description:
A GitHub projector issue/PR link: a GitHub issue/PR (`repo` full-name +
`issue_number`) projects into the `thread_id` in
`channel_id`/`workspace_id`, with inbound comments posted as `member_id`.
One Maidan thread per GitHub issue/PR.

disabled_at.description:
When egress to this issue/PR was disabled after an auth/config-class
failure. `None` = enabled; re-linking clears it. Ingress is unaffected —
the webhook keeps delivering comments.

GlossaryTerm.description:
A workspace's canonical definition of a term — the anti-drift pin so agents
use words the same way, and the target of the `defines` reference relation.
One entry per `(workspace_id, term)`. Flat by design (no hierarchy).

aliases.description: Alternate labels for the same term (SKOS altLabel).

harness.description: `None` for tasks whose usage named no harness.

HarnessRollup.description: The tasks mostly run by one harness.

HumanWait.description: A wait on a person as the board shows it.

returns_at.description: When an unanswered wait returns the thread to the queue.

since.description: When the holder declared it needs a person.

HumanWaitState.description:
Where an agent's wait on a person stands. The policy at the end is
locked: an unanswered wait returns the thread to the queue, and no
transition leads to a decision made on the person's behalf, because a
silence is not a yes.

ImportResult.description:
Result of a workspace import: the id of the workspace that now holds the
content (a fresh id in `new` mode, the bundle's id in `restore`).

refused.description:
Verified but refused by the allowlist. A non-zero count is
informational, not an error — see
[`IngestOutcome::SkippedNotFederatable`].

InstantiateRecipe.description:
Instantiate a recipe: `params` are validated against the recipe's declared
params (required ones must be present).

invite_token.description: The invite token, shown exactly once. Only its hash is stored.

signup_path.description: Where the invite link points, on this instance's origin.

consent.description:
The visitor agreed to be contacted about a place. A join without
consent is refused: the consent timestamp is the point of the row.

turnstile_token.description:
The Turnstile widget's token. Required when the instance runs
Turnstile, ignored otherwise.

use_case.description: What the visitor would use Maidan for, in their own words.

website.description:
Left empty by people. The page hides this field; a form-filling bot
fills it, and its join is answered like any other and not stored.

KindCensus.description:
EventKind distribution for a workspace (optionally narrowed to a channel
or thread). Zero-count kinds are omitted; [`KindCensus::total`] is the
denominator.

LandColor.description:
Land-gate vocabulary. Only [`LandColor::Green`] is a land.

* **green** — a qualifying LandGate pass; the FSM may `closed`.
* **amber** — flags-then-still-engages (accepted nonsense). Not a land.
* **red** — fail, pending requirement, or an unqualified pointer.

raw_land.description: The model's top choice before Maidan applies confidence policy.

recommended_land.description: Low-confidence green/red choices become amber (human review).

LandGateAdviceRequest.description:
A caller-supplied evaluation case. `state` is sent to TypeSafe only when
the feature is enabled and this endpoint is explicitly called.

oneOf.description:
Per-evaluation override. This cannot authorize a land: the response is
advisory and the existing qualified-verifier write remains mandatory.

LandGatePointer.description:
The pointer LandGate writes onto a thread. Small on purpose: kind,
pass/fail, optional artifact SHA, and the land color.

land.description:
Computed land color (not merely what LandGate wrote). Green only
when a qualifying pass exists, or when the gate is not armed.

landable.description: `land == green`. The FSM close-gate requires this when `required`.

required.description: A row exists — the gate is armed (require and/or a recorded pointer).

LandGateStatus.description: Pass/fail recorded on the thread by a gate-skilled verifier.

LandGateVerdict.description:
One verdict in a thread's land-gate history. The gate's standing holds the
latest pointer, and recording a new one replaces it; every recorded
pointer is also appended here and never changed, and clearing the gate
leaves the history in place.

id.description: Position in the history; increases with every verdict.

land.description: The land color the recorder wrote (not the computed standing).

oneOf.description: The delegate that recorded this verdict for `recorded_by`, when one did.

LegalHold.description:
A legal hold on a workspace. While held, the workspace's event-log and audit
rows are exempt from retention pruning, workspace
purge/erase is refused, and a message withdrawn (tombstoned) keeps its words
and earlier versions in [`PreservedMessage`] — evidence is preserved for
litigation. A workspace may be held for several matters at once, one hold
each; it is held while any hold remains, and what the holds kept is disposed
of only when the last is lifted.

lifted.description: `false` when the workspace was not suspended.

LinearClaimComments.description: Whether a workspace says its tasks' claims and releases on Linear.

LinkGithubIssue.description:
Link a GitHub issue/PR to a Maidan thread. `repo` is the `owner/name` full
name; `channel_id`/`workspace_id` are derived from the thread.

LinkSlackChannel.description:
Link a Slack channel to a Maidan thread. The link's channel and workspace
are derived from the thread; relayed messages are attributed to the
authenticated member.

LogSnapshot.description: Verified checkpoint a peer uses instead of a pruned prefix.

as_of_lsn.description: Workspace head included in this snapshot (`0` if the log is empty).

floor_lsn.description:
Oldest retained event id (`0` if empty). Catch-up after a cursor
strictly behind this floor is [`crate::CursorTooOld`].

ManagerDigest.description:
A member's unread followed-member lifecycle notifications since `since`,
composed into per-channel result/gate/stuck counts. This is a notification
view, not an analytics projection.

cost_per_completed_task_usd_micros.description: Lifetime cost per completed task. Absent when the workspace has none.

spend_usd_micros.description: Lifetime workspace spend in micro-USD. Not limited to `since`.

ManagerDigestChannel.description:
Notification-backed management rollup for one channel. `None` is the
workspace-level bucket (currently unattached approval gates).

MarkAllRead.description: Result of marking all of a member's notifications read.

MarkUnclaimable.description:
Body for `PUT /threads/:id/unclaimable` — park a thread from dispatch with a
reason (must be non-empty).

MemberConformance.description: One member's reports against the profile.

MemberEmail.description:
A member's delivery email address — where email notifications go. One per
member.

MemberFollow.description:
A member following another member's work occupancy. The follower receives
the followed member's relevant work-lifecycle notifications and may read a
live presence + assigned-work snapshot through the server surface. Presence
itself stays ephemeral; this row stores only the subscription edge.

MemberFreeze.description:
A frozen member. `frozen_by` is the operator/member who applied the freeze;
`reason` is a free-text note for the audit trail.

MemberOccupancy.description:
A followed member's live occupancy: ephemeral presence plus the currently
assigned, non-terminal work visible to the caller. Access filtering happens
at the transport boundary so private-channel threads never leak here.

MemberSkill.description:
A free-form skill tag a member (agent) declares. Skill routing matches a
task's required skills against a member's declared skills.

MemberWipView.description:
A member's WIP status: current live-claim count + the workspace limit
(`null` = unlimited).

MemoryBlock.description:
A labeled memory block. `value` is the whole content (a full-rewrite,
last-writer-wins field); `char_limit` (Letta's `limit`) bounds its length in
Unicode scalar values when set; `read_only` refuses writes; `owner_id` is the
member who owns the block.

MergeQueue.description: A pull request's merge-queue state, and why it was dequeued.

MergeQueueState.description: Where a pull request stands with the merge queue.

content.description:
Typed structured content; `None` for plain/legacy messages. `body` is
the plain-text projection of these blocks.

metadata.description:
Open annotation bag. Omitted from the wire when empty — most messages
carry no metadata, so `"metadata":{}` on every one was pure token waste.
Deserializes back to an empty object by default.

MessageBacklinks.description:
Incoming pointers at one message — the backlink index.

`references` is `list_references_to(Message, id)`
(`RelationKind` reverse edges, including `seeded_from`). Pins, reactions,
and votes are the other existing tables that point *at* the message.
Mentions are outgoing (the message points at members) and are not included.

MessageEdit.description: One recorded body change for a message.

MessageEditView.description:
A context-pack edit record. The before/after bodies are omitted unless the
caller asks (`include_edits`); the who/when/which-message signal stays.

MeterUsage.description: A workspace's month on one meter, against the allowance.

allowance.description: The instance allowance, when it sets one for this meter.

quantity.description: The month's sum for a counter, the latest measurement for a gauge.

capability_set.description:
Named set (`maidan.agent.worker` / `maidan.human.admin`). Combined
with `capabilities` this is progressive grant: requested ⊆ set.

secret.description: Returned once. Only its SHA-256 hash is persisted.

ModelEffortOutcome.description: One model and effort inside a task class.

effort.description: Absent when the reports did not name an effort.

tasks.description: Threads that ran on only this model and effort.

usd_micros.description: Spend on every one of those threads, completed or not.

usd_micros_per_completed_task.description: `usd_micros` over `completed_tasks`, rounded up; absent with none.

ModelRequestView.description:
Who a model asked through, and whose confirmation it is waiting for. The
link itself is never listed: only the person it was issued to has it.

client_id.description: The credential client's id, when `client_source` is `credential`.

client_source.description:
Where `client_name` came from: the credential, the client's own
`clientInfo` (self-reported), or nowhere.

member_id.description: The member whose credential the model used, the one who can confirm.

MonthlyUsage.description: A workspace's usage for one UTC month.

Notification.description:
A per-recipient notification. Where a mention is one shared
`maidan_mentions` row read through a single inbox cursor, this is one row
per (recipient, source event): *who* should know, *what* triggered it
(`kind` = the source [`EventKind`] + `source_log_id` = the event-log row),
denormalized context (`channel/thread/message/actor`) so the inbox renders
without re-fetching the event, and per-recipient read state. The
zero-blast-radius foundation for the notification router + unified inbox
that follow — nothing writes rows yet.

oneOf.description: Who caused it (e.g. the mentioner), when applicable.

snoozed_until.description:
Snoozed until this instant — while in the future the notification is
hidden from the default inbox + badge, then resurfaces. `None` = not
snoozed. Orthogonal to `read_at`.

source_log_id.description: The `maidan_events` row that triggered this notification.

NotificationPref.description:
A member's notification preference for one event kind. `muted` suppresses
router-written notifications of `kind` for this member; the absence of a row
is the default (notify). The routing brain the notification router consults
before writing.

NotificationThreadGroup.description:
A member's notifications for one thread, collapsed. The grouped inbox shows
one row per thread — the newest notification plus how many (and how many
unread) it stands for — so a busy thread doesn't flood the flat list.
`thread_id` is `None` for the group of notifications that carry no thread.

latest.description: The newest notification in the group (its `created_at` orders the groups).

OAuthErrorBody.description: The body of an OAuth error response.

OAuthGrantView.description:
One grant as the member sees it. `client_name` comes from the
client's registry row (a metadata-document client gets its row on
first use at `/authorize`); it is absent only for a row that predates
the name being recorded, and then the grant shows by client id alone.

client_id.description: Required unless the client authenticates with HTTP Basic.

token.description: The access token or refresh token to revoke.

token_type_hint.description:
`access_token` or `refresh_token`: where to look first. Both kinds are
looked up whatever it says (RFC 7009 section 2.1).

OAuthTokenRequest.description:
Every parameter either grant reads. All optional, so a missing one is an
`invalid_request` naming it rather than a deserialization failure.

client_id.description: Required unless the client authenticates with HTTP Basic.

redirect_uri.description: The redirect URI the code was issued for (`authorization_code`).

resource.description:
RFC 8707 resource indicator: must be the MCP endpoint,
`<MAIDAN_PUBLIC_ORIGIN>/mcp/streamable`.

scope.description:
Space-delimited; on `refresh_token` it may narrow the grant's scope,
never widen it.

phase.description:
`serving`, `degraded` (a readiness check fails) or `draining` (SIGTERM
received; the listener closes after the drain delay).

oneOf.description: `None` without a read replica.

OrphanToolResult.description:
A `ToolResult` block whose `tool_use_id` matched no `ToolUse` in the scanned
messages — surfaced rather than dropped so a gap is visible.

PackElision.description:
An auditable record of the messages a context pack dropped to fit its token
budget. The pack keeps the thread's opening message (framing) and its
most-recent tail; the elided middle is summarized here, so the omission is
visible in the response and recoverable (page from `first_elided_id`, or
refetch the thread without a budget).

elided_token_estimate.description: Estimated tokens the elided messages would have cost.

first_elided_id.description: The oldest elided message — page from here to recover the middle.

summary.description: A human/agent-readable summary naming the omission and how to recover it.

ParentGrounding.description:
Grounding for a **child** thread's context pack: a compact orientation to
the parent it was spawned from, so a fresh claimer of a sub-task knows *why
it exists* (the parent's opening ask) and *what the parent concluded* (its
latest recorded decision). Deliberately bounded — one framing message plus
one decision payload, not the parent's whole history.

latest_result.description: The parent's latest recorded decision/result payload, if any.

oneOf.description: The parent's opening (oldest) message — the framing / task statement.

PauseRepo.description:
The body of a pause: the repository, in any spelling [`normalize_repo`]
accepts, and an optional note for the audit trail.

PayerStamp.description: Immutable attribution carried by the usage ledger and `UsageReported`.

PlaceLegalHold.description:
Body for `POST /workspaces/:id/legal-holds` — place a legal hold. `reason` is
required (non-empty).

PlanAmendment.description: What an amendment did, as the amend routes answer.

amendments.description: Amendments this plan has taken, this one included.

held.description: The added children are held for review with the rest of the plan.

rewired.description:
Keys whose dependencies changed: the rewired ones, and those that
waited for a cancelled or replaced child.

PlanChild.description: One child of a plan, as the planner submits it.

oneOf.description: Kind, engine, size and acceptance, as at intake.

depends_on.description: Keys of children in the same plan this one waits for.

test.description:
The command that proves the child done (`cargo test -p x`). A plan
submitted through the API must give one; it is kept at the end of the
child's description, where its worker reads it.

PlanChildren.description: The children a plan made, as the plan routes answer.

held.description:
The plan is held for review: its children wait, blocked, until a
Maintainer releases it.

PlanRelease.description: The children a plan release made claimable.

PlanRewire.description: A new `depends_on` for a child already in the plan.

depends_on.description: The keys it waits for from now on, replacing the ones it had.

PlanState.description: How far a plan parent's children have got.

blocked.description:
Open children held back by a block row (a dependency that closed
without landing, or any other block).

PlannedChild.description: A child the plan made, by key.

PreservedMessage.description:
What a legal hold kept of a message withdrawn while the workspace was held:
its last words and every earlier version. The member's view is unchanged —
the message is gone everywhere they look. Read only through the audited
preserved-content read; lifting the hold deletes it.

PriceSnapshot.description:
Immutable prices used for one report, in micro-USD per million tokens.

Maidan preserves this reporter-supplied evidence; it is not a live vendor
rate card. The write tiers are priced apart so a 5-minute write and a
1-hour write are not charged as one rate.

ProblemDetails.description:
RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`; 9457 obsoletes 7807
and keeps its format).

children.description: On a `plan-conflict` 409: the children the plan already has.

conflicts.description:
On a `footprint-conflict` 409: the live claim items the footprint
overlaps, each with its thread, holder and lease.

must_refetch.description: A CursorTooOld 409 is a must-refetch, never a silent clamp.

quota_bytes.description: On a `media-quota-exceeded` 409: the workspace's media quota.

snapshot.description:
GET this path for a hashed snapshot covering the pruned prefix, then
catch up from `as_of_lsn`.

upload_bytes.description: On a `media-quota-exceeded` 409: the size of the refused upload.

used_bytes.description:
On a `media-quota-exceeded` 409: the bytes of media the workspace
holds.

ProtectedResourceMetadata.description:
RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata for the MCP endpoint.

No `scopes_supported`: a client treats it as the set it may request, and
the set a member can delegate is their own capabilities intersected with
the client's allowed scopes, so there is no server-wide set to name.

provider.description: `None` for tasks whose usage named no provider.

ProviderRollup.description: The tasks whose spend was mostly with one model provider.

ProvisionWorkspace.description:
Body for `POST /operator/workspaces`. Opens another workspace and its first
admin. Both fields are trimmed. Blank is a 400 after the capability check,
so a body of `{}` still reaches it.

PullCi.description:
Where the checks on a tracked pull request stand, as the change sweep last
read them.

failing_jobs.description: The checks that failed on this head, at most 20.

gate_reasons.description:
What holds the pull request back; empty when nothing the sweep reads
does.

head_sha.description: The head commit the checks ran on.

log_tail.description:
The last 4 KB of the first failing job's log, when GitHub Actions ran
it. Read once, when the head first fails.

oneOf.description: Where the pull request stands with its base branch's merge queue.

merge_state.description:
GitHub's merge state for the pull request (`CLEAN`, `BEHIND`,
`BLOCKED`, `DIRTY`, `DRAFT`, `UNSTABLE`, ...), when GitHub had one.

missing_checks.description:
Checks the base branch's protection requires that never reported on
this head, though every check that did report has finished.

unresolved_thread_links.description: Where the first unresolved review threads are, at most 20.

unresolved_threads.description:
How many review threads are unresolved, bots' (a review bot's) as
well as people's.

updated_at.description: When the sweep last read it.

PushKeys.description: The keys of a browser `PushSubscription` — base64url.

PushSubscription.description:
A member's Web Push subscription — one browser/device. From the browser's
`PushManager.subscribe()`: `endpoint` is the push service URL, `p256dh` the
subscription's public ECDH key and `auth` its auth secret (both base64url).
The notification router delivers a Web Push message to `endpoint` when the
member has no live WebSocket connection.

QueueDepth.description:
A channel's task-queue depth — a point-in-time partition of its
**open** (non-terminal, non-tombstoned) task threads, for an orchestrator
deciding whether to scale workers. The four sub-counts partition `open`:
- `assigned`: actively held (an assignee with a live, non-expired lease).
- `ready`: claimable now, exactly what `claim_next` would hand to a claimer
  with no skill, repository or engine restriction. Not held (or its lease
  lapsed) and not blocked or unclaimable.
- `blocked`: not held but stalled on something that clears: an explicit
  block, a non-terminal dependency, a pending approval gate, or a footprint
  conflict.
- `unclaimable`: not held but withheld until someone acts: parked from
  dispatch, at its budget, or already holding a result it was not
  re-queued after. Takes precedence over `blocked`.

outbox_pending.description: `None` when no transactional outbox is configured.

Recipe.description:
A stored recipe blueprint. `spec` is the frozen [`RecipeSpec`]; identity and
the target channel are the only first-class columns.

RecipeChild.description:
An inline child sub-task. `key` is a spec-local handle (referenced by other
children's `depends_on`); `required_skills` attach to the created child
thread so `claim_next` routes it; `depends_on` are the keys of sibling
children this one waits on.

RecipeParam.description: A named parameter a recipe consumes at instantiation.

RecipeRetry.description:
A retry policy carried in the snapshot (not enforced by the room — a claimer
or producer reads it). `max_attempts` is advisory.

RecipeRun.description:
A single instantiation of a recipe — the copy-on-fire record. `spec_snapshot`
freezes the recipe bytes at fire time so a later edit to the recipe never
changes what this run was, and `root_thread_id` is the parent thread created.

RecipeSpec.description:
The recipe blueprint: params, a definition of done, a retry policy, and the
inline child sub-tasks (a DAG). Serialized as the `spec` JSON column.

children.description:
Inline child sub-tasks. Each becomes a child thread of the instantiated
parent; `depends_on` wires the readiness DAG among them.

relation.description:
The typed predicate. Wire form is a snake_case string; the controlled
set is [`RelationKind::CONTROLLED`], unknown values round-trip via
[`RelationKind::Other`].

RegisterPull.description:
A pull request the change flow did not open (a session's), registered
on its task's thread so the swarm metrics track it.

claimed_at.description:
When the task was claimed, for a claim said outside Maidan; a
`CLAIM:` comment Maidan posted takes precedence.

RegisteredPull.description: A registered pull request as tracked.

opened_at.description:
Where its time to ready starts: the task's `CLAIM:` comment, else the
`claimed_at` given, else when it was registered.

ReindexJob.description:
An embedding reindex job, persisted so its status is visible on any replica
and survives restart. `job_id`/`workspace_id` are raw UUIDs to match the
operator HTTP shape.

RelationKind.description: A relation name: supports, refutes, defines, depends, duplicates, grounds, supersedes, seeded_from, or any other string

ReleaseClaim.description:
Release a claim (graceful handoff): the current holder returns the thread to
the queue by presenting its fencing token.

RenameThread.description:
Rename a thread. The title is required and non-empty — a rename gives the
thread a name, so a blank title is rejected.

RenameWorkspace.description:
Body for `PATCH /workspaces/:id`. Sets the display name. The workspace id
stays. Trimmed; 1 to 200 characters.

name.description:
Omitted or blank is a 400 once the caller has `workspace:write`.
Defaulted so a body of `{}` still reaches the capability check.

RenewClaim.description:
Extend a claimed thread's lease, for the current assignee holding the
matching fencing token. `claim_lease_id` is the value returned in the
claiming response's `Thread.claim_lease_id`; a stale holder whose claim was
reclaimed presents an outdated token and is rejected.

lease_secs.description: The new lease, in seconds from now (1 s to 7 days).

RepoPause.description:
A repository paused in one workspace: no thread whose footprint names it
is claimed until the pause is lifted.

by_engine.description:
By the engine each task was routed to, in engine order with unrouted
tasks last.

by_harness.description: By the harness that ran each task, most tasks first, unnamed last.

by_provider.description:
By the provider that spent the most on each task, most tasks first,
unnamed last: so providers are compared as well as engines.

by_risk.description:
By risk tier, standard first. Slices with no tasks are omitted from
every split.

by_size.description: By size, `S` to `L` with unsized tasks last.

by_tier.description: By review tier, `A` then `B`, with untiered tasks counted as `B`.

RepoRollup.description:
One repository's rollup. Pi is given small and medium work and sessions
the risky work, so an engine comparison is read within a size or a risk
tier, not across the whole repository.

armed_revision.description:
The newest `ThreadResult::produced_at` this row has accepted. Monotonic:
arming only ever moves it forward, which is the dedup.

delivered_revision.description:
The newest revision that actually reached the surface. `None` = never
delivered.

external_ref.description:
The external object we created, if we could address it — a Slack `ts`, a
GitHub comment id. `None` means "post next time", with the hidden body
marker as the recovery path rather than a guess.

head_sha.description:
The commit a `github_branch` delivery landed, decoded from the same
handle as [`Self::pr_number`].

pr_number.description:
The pull request a `github_branch` delivery landed as, decoded from the
`<commit_sha>#<pull_number>` handle in [`Self::external_ref`]. `None`
for every other surface, and for a branch row whose handle does not
decode. Derived when a row is materialized from storage (see
[`Self::derive_pull_fields`]); never persisted.

pr_url.description:
The pull request's web URL, built from the target's repository and
[`Self::pr_number`]. Derived alongside it; `None` whenever it is.

template_warnings.description:
For a change: what its pull request lacks against the producer's
template (`missing_testing`, `missing_issue_key`). A flag, not a
failure: the change landed either way. Absent when nothing is missing.

ResultEvidence.description:
The result a review packet pins: the hash of its canonical JSON and who
produced it.

media_days.description:
Days a media artifact (attachment, screenshot, recording) is kept once
nothing in the workspace references it. The instance's comes from
`MAIDAN_RETENTION_MEDIA_DAYS` (30 unless set).

media_quota_bytes.description:
Bytes of media artifacts the workspace may hold. An upload that would
go past it is refused with a `media-quota-exceeded` 409. The
instance's comes from `MAIDAN_MEDIA_QUOTA_BYTES` (20 GiB unless set).

RetentionPolicy.description:
A workspace's retention as `GET /workspaces/{id}/retention` reports it: what
the workspace set, what the instance keeps, and what is pruned in effect
(the shorter of the two per kind).

ReviewChildren.description: Whether a change entering review spawns its second-family review child.

ReviewDecision.description: A reviewer's decision on a thread.

ReviewPacket.description:
An immutable record of one hand-off to review: who started the review, the
manifest of what it was handed, and that manifest's root. Each
`start_review` writes one; nothing updates it.

self_reported_only.description:
The server's warning: approving this packet would rest on
self-reported evidence only. Derived from `manifest.attestations`.

thread_version.description:
The thread's version at the hand-off: how many writes its content had
seen, messages included. A later version means the thread moved on.

ReviewStatus.description:
The computed review standing of a thread — what the close-gate reads for the
**approval** side (the `refutes`-edge block is checked separately at the gate).

approvals.description:
Distinct **qualifying** approvals: decision = approve, reviewer is neither
owner nor assignee, and (when a named reviewer set exists) is in it.

approvals_met.description:
Whether the approval requirement is met (`required_count == 0` or
`approvals >= required_count`).

required_count.description: Approvals required (0 when no requirement is set).

ReviewThreadLink.description: Where an unresolved review thread is, and who opened it.

author.description: The login of the first comment's author, a bot's included.

ReviewVerdict.description:
One verdict in a thread's review history. [`ThreadReview`] holds each
reviewer's current decision, and re-submitting replaces it; every
submission is also appended here and never changed, so an owner can see
the sequence of verdicts that led to a land.

oneOf.description: The delegate that submitted this verdict for `reviewer_id`, when one did.

head_sha.description: The full head SHA of the change this verdict was given against.

id.description: Position in the history; increases with every verdict.

RevokeOAuthGrantResponse.description: What a revoke ended, counted by the lineage revocation itself.

threat_model.description: Whether the tasks were marked as touching the threat model.

RiskRollup.description: The tasks of one risk tier.

RoomCard.description: Authenticated room card: stable id + current handle + canonical URI.

RoomDiscovery.description:
Public `/.well-known/maidan-room` document. Scheme only — no
workspace list (that would leak tenants).

RunOccupancy.description:
Occupancy of every **open** thread that shares a `parent_run_id` — the
nested-attribution view of [`ChannelOccupancy`].

Same four buckets (`queued` / `claimed` / `working` / `blocked` partition
`open`). Scoped to a workspace so two tenants cannot collide on a producer
id. F7 mute is not consulted: muted nested work still counts.

SearchHit.description:
Search hit (`GET /workspaces/{wid}/search`). `rank` is backend-specific
(higher is better within one response). `score` is normalized to `[0, 1]`
and comparable across Postgres and SQLite within the same `mode`.

score.description: Normalized relevance in `[0, 1]`; comparable across backends within one mode.

backfill_percent.description:
`tap_cursor` as a share of the head, `100.0` for an empty log. Below 100
right after a rebuild means the backfill is still running.

behind.description: Events the search tap has not projected yet.

event_log_head.description: Highest event-log id on the instance.

tap_cursor.description: Where the search tap last finished.

Secret.description:
A stored secret's **metadata** — never its value. Listing secrets returns
these; the value is a separate, capability-gated resolve.

SecretEgressHost.description:
A host a workspace trusts to receive its secret values: on egress to this
host the broker substitutes `secret://<name>` refs from this workspace's
secrets. Listing it is granting that host every secret the payload names,
so the list is per workspace and starts empty.

host.description: Lowercase hostname or IPv4 address, no scheme or port.

SecretValue.description:
A resolved secret value — the `resolve` response body. This is the only
place a secret value crosses the wire out of Maidan.

SeedFromMessage.description:
Seed a new work thread from a source message — the write side of "re-ask".
`inclusion`: `pointer` (default, lineage edge only) or `quote` (the seed's
first message quotes the source). `channel_id` defaults to the source's
channel. The seed is a titled, claimable child; the source is untouched;
lineage is a `seeded_from` reference edge (new thread → source message).

display_name.description:
Display name of the signed-in member, when one is set. `null` when the
member has none. The id stays in `member_id`.

oneOf.description:
The token a session made by `POST /auth/session/from-token` holds the
authority of; `null` for an OIDC session.

SessionWorkspace.description: One workspace the signed-in person can switch to.

current.description: `true` for the workspace this session is in.

member_id.description: The person's member in that workspace.

name.description: The workspace's display name (a label, not an address).

SessionWorkspaces.description:
`GET /auth/session/workspaces`: the session's own workspace first, then
every other workspace the identity it signed in with is a member of,
newest sign-in first, at most 200.

SetApprovalPolicy.description:
Body for `PUT /workspaces/:id/approval-policy`. It replaces the whole
policy: a field left out or `null` is back on its default, and with both
left out the workspace has no policy of its own.

oneOf.description:
The lowest gate risk at which a model's accept through
`approval_decide` needs a person's confirmation. Default `low`.

confirm_link_ttl_seconds.description:
How long a confirmation link lives, in seconds: 60 to 3600. Default
600. A link already sent keeps the lifetime it was minted with.

SetDelegationPolicy.description:
Body for `PUT /workspaces/:wid/delegation-policy`. `max_grant_days` is the
longest a delegation grant may live (1–3650); `null` restores the default,
90 days.

SetDeliveryMode.description:
Set a member's email delivery mode. An unknown `mode` fails deserialization
→ `400`.

SetEmail.description: Set a member's delivery email address.

SetGlossaryTerm.description:
Define (or redefine) a glossary term. The term itself is the path segment;
this is the body. `aliases` defaults to empty when omitted.

SetLandGate.description:
Record a LandGate pointer. `land` is optional — a fail is always red; a pass
defaults to green; amber is flags-then-still-engages and is not a land.

SetMemberDisplayName.description:
Body for `PATCH /members/:id`. Sets the member's display name; a blank
name clears it.
Defaulted so a body of `{}` still reaches the capability check.

SetMemoryBlockValue.description:
Full-rewrite a memory block's value. A read-only block or a value over the
block's char limit is rejected (400).

SetNotificationPref.description: Set a member's mute preference for one event kind.

SetReviewRequirement.description:
Set a thread's review requirement: `required_count` distinct qualifying
approvals before it can `close`.

SetSlotCapacity.description: The body that sets a slot's capacity.

capacity.description: At least 1: how many live claims may hold the slot at once.

SetSpawnBudget.description:
Body for `PUT /workspaces/:id/spawn-budget` — the workspace's cap on agent
fan-out. A full replace: an omitted or `null` axis is unlimited, so `{}`
clears the budget. `0` freezes an axis.

max_children.description: Max direct child threads per parent.

max_depth.description: Max thread nesting depth (a root thread is depth 1).

max_tools.description: Max tool calls recorded on one thread.

SetThreadBlock.description:
Body for `PUT /threads/:id/block` — set an explicit dispatch block. `reason`
is the closed `BlockedReason` enum
(`dag|gate|human|child|quota|unclaimable`); unknown → 400 at the extractor.

note.description: Human-readable note explaining why the thread is blocked.

SetThreadLineage.description:
Home a producer's `run_id` on a thread as `parent_run_id`. The value is the
producer's string — Maidan does not mint a parallel id.

SetThreadOwner.description:
Set a thread's durable owner — the accountable party, distinct from the
assignee/claimer.

SetThreadPriority.description:
Body for `PUT /threads/:id/priority` — set a thread's dispatch priority.
Higher = more urgent; the default is 0.

SetThreadResult.description:
Set a task's structured result. `result` is arbitrary JSON.
`claim_lease_id` is the caller's live claim on the thread (the claim
response's `thread.claim_lease_id`); a lease that lapsed and was taken
over, or was released, is refused 409 `claim-lost` and nothing is stored.

SetThreadSteer.description: Set a thread's persisted steer — durable steering guidance.

SetThreadWait.description:
Body for `PUT /threads/:id/wait` — set a wait timer. On `wait_until` the
sweeper escalates via `on_timeout` (default `notify`); an optional `reason`
records why the thread is waiting.

SetWipLimit.description:
Body for `PUT /workspaces/:wid/wip-limit`. `limit: null` clears the cap
(unlimited); a value caps concurrent live claims per member (`0` freezes
claiming).

owner_id.description: Internal member accountable for the external share.

oneOf.description: The size the planner gave the tasks; `None` for tasks never sized.

SlackChannelLink.description:
A Slack projector channel link: a Slack channel projects into the
`thread_id` in `channel_id`/`workspace_id`, with inbound Slack messages
posted as `member_id`. One Maidan thread per Slack channel.

disabled_at.description:
When egress to this channel was disabled after an auth/config-class
failure. `None` = enabled; re-linking clears it. Ingress is unaffected —
a revoked *write* scope does not stop Slack from reaching us.

SliceNumbers.description: How a set of tasks did: a whole repository, or one slice of it.

cost_usd_micros_per_merged.description:
Total cost of the tasks over the merged ones; `None` before the first
merge.

first_ci_pass_rate.description:
Tasks whose first delivered head passed CI, over those whose first
head's checks finished; `None` with none finished.

followup_fix_rate.description: `followup_fixed` over the same known merged tasks.

followup_fixed.description: Merged tasks a later pull request said it fixed.

mean_human_commits.description: Mean commits a person added, over merged tasks read so far.

mean_sent_back.description: Reviews that sent work back, per task.

misrouted.description:
Tasks the engine they were routed to could not finish: flagged
non-converging while open, or closed unmerged after reaching the
round limit.

revert_rate.description:
`reverted` over the merged tasks whose outcome is known: reverted,
followed by a fix, or merged over [`OUTCOME_WINDOW_DAYS`] ago. `None`
with none known.

SlotUsage.description:
A slot in a workspace: its capacity, when an operator set one, and how
many live claims hold it now.

capacity.description: `None` for a slot in use that has no capacity, which limits nothing.

SnoozeNotification.description: Snooze a notification until this RFC 3339 instant.

SpawnBudgetView.description: The workspace's spawn budget; a `null` axis is unlimited.

StoredEvent.description:
OpenAPI / utoipa shape of [`StoredEvent`]: the durable columns plus the
wire-only `$type` this type still defers.

$type.description: Observable lexicon type. Computed from `kind` on serialize. Not stored.

content_key.description:
Base64 key that opens `payload.sealed`. Only on whole-log reads (a
federation peer, catch-up) and only while the words are live. A
`sealed` block without it means the words were shredded.

traceparent.description: W3C `traceparent` of the server span that wrote the event. Not hashed.

StrongRef.description:
Content-addressed pin. `uri` names the object; `content_hash` is
`sha256:<hex>` of its canonical JSON (or of the log event that
committed it).

SubmitPlan.description: A plan as submitted: the planner's claim on the parent and the children.

lease_id.description:
The parent's `claim_lease_id`: only the planner holding the parent's
live claim may plan it.

SubmitReview.description:
Submit a review decision. The reviewer is the caller; an owner/assignee may
submit but it won't count toward the requirement.

evidence_root.description:
The `evidence_root` of the review packet being decided on
(`GET /threads/{id}/review-packet`). Required to approve.

reason.description: Why, for the audit log and for the workspace's own operators.

SwarmMetrics.description: The ramp metrics for a workspace.

TaskAttributes.description: A thread's task attributes, whole: setting them replaces every field.

acceptance.description:
How a reviewer verifies the task: what the change must satisfy. Shown
to the worker in the thread context.

oneOf.description:
The service lane the task may run in: batch or flex for work whose
deadline has slack, unset for realtime.

linear_issue.description:
The Linear issue the task is for (`ENG-1234`). Where the workspace
has turned claim comments on, the task's claim and release are said
on it.

review_family.description:
The provider family a review child is routed to: one other than the
family of the change's author, picked when the change entered review.
Set by the server only; setting attributes leaves it as it was.

oneOf.description:
The change's review tier, set at intake and restated when a new head
changes it. Read by the metrics only; nothing routes or gates on it.

TaskClassOutcomes.description: One task class: a thread kind and size.

outcomes.description:
Cheapest first by cost per completed task; combinations with no
completed task last.

size.description: Absent for threads with no size set.

oneOf.description: Absent until some combination has `min_completed` completed tasks.

switched_tasks.description:
Threads whose reports named more than one model or effort. Left out
of `outcomes`.

TaskClassRouting.description: Every task class in a workspace with ledger evidence.

TaskEngine.description:
Who or what a task is meant for. `None` on a thread means nobody has
routed it yet; an engine-filtered claim never takes a thread routed to
another engine, nor one not routed at all. A workspace's default engine
routes the threads created there without one.

TaskFingerprint.description:
A task's stored fingerprint, and the earlier open task with the same
fingerprint in the same workspace that it was linked to when created.

oneOf.description:
The oldest live task in the workspace that was open or in review
with the same fingerprint when this one was created. `None` when
there was none.

TaskFlag.description: Why a task needs a look.

TaskKind.description: What kind of work a task is.

TaskLane.description:
The service lane a thread's model calls may run in (Context Economics
C7). A thread whose deadline has slack can be marked for a provider's
batch API (about half price, results within hours) or its flex tier
(discounted, slower, may be refused under load). Unset is the realtime
lane, the default.

attributes.description:
The task's attributes; the defaults when the thread was never
described.

claim_lapses.description: Claims that lapsed before the work was handed in.

claim_to_first_delivery_secs.description: First claim to the first round delivered, in seconds.

claimed_at.description:
When the thread was first assigned: a claim, or a person assigning
it by hand.

oneOf.description: How the checks stood on the first delivered head.

followup_fixes.description: Later merged pull requests that say they fix this one.

handed_off.description: Handed to a session at `non_converging`: counted as misrouted.

harness.description:
The harness that ran the work and spent the most (`claude-code`,
`cursor`, `codex`, `pi`, ...), as its usage reports named it.

human_commits.description:
Commits on the pull request the change flow did not deliver: a proxy
for a person's edits. `None` until read after the merge.

human_reviews.description:
Reviews and review comments by accounts that are not bots: a proxy
for review effort, which GitHub cannot time.

linear_issue.description: The Linear issue the change is for, when known.

merged_without_edits.description:
Whether the merged head was the last commit the change flow
delivered, so nobody else pushed to it; `None` until merged.

provider.description:
The model provider that spent the most on the task (`anthropic`,
`openai`, `xai`, ...), as its usage reports named it.

rebases.description: How many of the rounds were squash-rebases.

reverted.description: Whether a revert of it landed on the base; `None` until merged.

review_wait_secs.description:
From the first green CI on a head (else the first move to review) to
the first review submitted, in seconds: how long finished work waited
for a reviewer, not for CI.

sent_back.description: Reviews that sent the work back.

time_to_first_human_review_secs.description: From ready (else opened) to the first human review or review comment.

TaskSchedule.description:
A schedule that materializes a task thread when due. A one-shot
(`interval_secs == None`) fires once then deactivates; a recurring schedule
(`interval_secs == Some(n)`) re-arms `next_run_at += n s` after each firing.
The background sweeper (a later cluster) creates a thread titled `title` in
`channel_id` when `active && next_run_at <= now`.

oneOf.description:
When set, firing this schedule instantiates the recipe (parent + DAG
children, copy-on-fire) instead of creating one bare thread.

TaskSize.description: How big a task is, as its planner judged it.

TaskTier.description:
How much review a change needs before it merges: Tier A takes the fast
path, Tier B a full review. A thread with no tier stored counts as B in
the metrics, while the stored value stays unset, so a later restatement
can tell "never said" from "B".

oneOf.description:
The member this thread/task is assigned to, if any. An axis orthogonal
to [`ThreadState`]: assignment persists across state transitions. Set
via assign/handoff, atomic claim, or cleared on unassign.

assignment_expires_at.description:
Lease deadline for a claimed assignment. When set and in the past, the
assignment is reclaimable by the next `claim_next` (dead-agent
recovery); `None` is a durable assignment with no lease.

oneOf.description:
The thread's task attributes (kind, engine, threat model). Populated
by the API layer on the reads that report them; `None` in store-level
queries that do not read the attributes table. A thread with no
attributes row reads as [`TaskAttributes::default`] where they are
reported.

The thread's explicit dispatch block, if any. Populated by the API
layer when returning thread details; `None` in store-level queries
that do not JOIN the blocks table.

ci.description:
Where the checks stand on each pull request tracked on the thread, as
the change sweep last read them while it was open. Read by a single-thread
read; empty on the list reads.

oneOf.description:
The fencing value for the current claim. A fresh resource-version minted
every time `assignee_id` is set (claim / claim_next / assign) and
cleared on unassign. `renew_claim` and other claim-holder operations
must present the matching value — a TTL lease alone lets a stale holder
act after the next owner has taken over.

closed_without_review.description:
The thread is closed (or archived) and no approval stands on it. The
review gate is opt-in, so a close can need none; the board says so
rather than showing a plain "done". Read by a single-thread read and a
channel's thread page, the reads a board makes; `false` on the other
list reads.

oneOf.description:
The member who created this thread, if a member did. Unlike
[`Thread::owner_id`] it never changes; it is the producer whose own
task this is, so it may cancel it without `thread:transition`.

description.description:
What the task is about, in the creator's words. Set at creation;
`None` on threads created before descriptions existed.

oneOf.description:
Where a thread whose holder is waiting on a person stands: the
holder of a live, acknowledged lease declared `needs_input` or
`needs_review` and no person has answered yet. Set by the board's
reads; `None` elsewhere and when nobody is waiting on a person.

last_progress_at.description:
When the holder of a live, acknowledged lease last showed progress:
the latest of its acknowledgement, its last message on the thread and
its active status declaration. A lease renewal is not progress, since
a hung agent's heartbeat keeps renewing. Read by the board's reads (a
single-thread read and a channel's thread page); `None` elsewhere and
on threads nobody is working.

notices.description:
The change notices on the thread, newest first, at most 10. Read by a
single-thread read, so a worker sees "rebase before you deliver" with
the thread; empty on the list reads.

oneOf.description:
The durable OWNER of this task/thread: the accountable party — a human,
typically — distinct from the [`Thread::assignee_id`] claimer that does
the work. Orthogonal to the FSM and the claim axis. The owner receives
stuck notifications and, once set, opts the thread into
separation-of-duties (the claimer cannot land its own work). `None` = no
designated owner (unrestricted).

On a plan parent, how far its children have got. Read by a
single-thread read only; absent on lists and on threads that are not
plans with children.

stalled.description:
System-computed and never declarable: the holder has shown no progress
for `MAIDAN_STALL_SECS` and has not said it is waiting. Set by the
board's reads from [`Thread::last_progress_at`].

oneOf.description:
The agent's self-reported status, if declared. Set via `declare_status`;
cleared on human response. `None` = no active declaration.

work_started_at.description:
The working clock. `assignment_expires_at` is the *claim* clock (lease
deadline); this is when the current holder acknowledged and began work
(`acknowledge_claim`). `None` = claimed but not yet started, or
unassigned. Reset to `None` on every (re)claim/assign/unassign so it
always reflects the CURRENT claim epoch — letting occupancy separate a
claimed-but-idle agent from one actively working.

ThreadArtifact.description: An artifact linked to a thread as evidence, by content hash.

ThreadBlock.description:
An explicit dispatch block on a thread: while this exists, `claim_next`
skips the thread. One block per thread (upsert). Clearing the row is the
unblock — later clusters emit `BlockedResolved`.

note.description:
Human-readable note explaining why the thread is blocked. Set by
`set_thread_block`; empty when the blocker gave no note.

ThreadBrief.description:
What working a thread does not change: a post, a claim or a renewal leaves
it as it was, so it belongs in the cached prefix. State and the lease are
in the tail.

oneOf.description:
The task's attributes (kind, engine, size, acceptance, Linear issue),
so the worker reading the pack sees what it is asked to do and how it
is checked. Absent from an as-of pack: they are current routing state,
not history.
The accountable party (see [`Thread::owner_id`]).

required_skills.description:
Skills a claimer must hold, sorted. Absent from an as-of pack: the
event log does not record them.

ThreadBudget.description:
A per-thread budget envelope. An orchestrator sets any of the optional
maxima; an agent reports incremental usage as it works, and when a dimension
is exceeded the run is stopped (the claim fails → DLQ). USD is integer
micros ($1 = 1_000_000) to keep money out of floats. Wall time is measured,
never reported: the live claim's share comes from the thread's working clock
(`work_started_at`), and `used_wall_secs` holds what earlier claims worked
before they ended. A lapsed lease is charged through its deadline; every
other ending is charged through the moment it ended.

used_cache_read_tokens.description:
Cache reads. Counted in `used_usd_micros` at their price, not in
`used_tokens` / `max_tokens`.

used_input_tokens.description:
Uncached input charged on this thread. `used_tokens` is the fresh sum,
not this column.

used_wall_secs.description:
Seconds worked by earlier claims on this thread, from each one's
acknowledgement to the moment that claim ended. A lapsed lease ends at
its deadline. Counted against `max_wall_secs` together with the live
claim's working time.

ThreadCancellation.description: The record of a cancel, kept so a repeat answers with the first one.

ThreadClaimResult.description:
Outcome of an atomic [`Thread`] claim: `claimed` is `true` when this call
won the compare-and-set (the thread was unassigned and is now the caller's),
`false` when it was already assigned. `thread` is the current row either
way.

ThreadContext.description:
A thread context pack. It serializes as one JSON object: the prefix fields,
then the tail fields. REST serves these bytes. MCP serves the prefix and
the tail as two content parts. A snapshot stores these bytes, so the same
state has one sha256 everywhere.

ThreadDependenciesView.description: A task's dependency edges plus whether it is ready to run.

ready.description:
